name: Household Carpet Cleaner
definition: A household upright extraction appliance that dispenses cleaning liquid into carpet, provides mechanical agitation where designed, and recovers dirty liquid into a separate tank.
includedScope: Uprights with documented hose and upholstery tools
excludedScope: Portable spot-only cleaners and commercial extractors
Dry vacuums, hard-floor wet-dry cleaners and steam-only appliances
primaryApplications: Approved rugs, stairs and upholstery with model-specific tools
headline: Household carpet cleaner tanks, brushes, solutions and buyer checks
description: This profile separates solution delivery, agitation, suction recovery, clean and dirty tanks, hose tools, drying claims and maintenance so buyers can compare household carpet cleaners without assuming every textile or detergent is compatible.
metaDescription: Household carpet cleaner guide covering upright types, tanks, brushes, solutions, models, tests and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not textile, chemical, hygiene or electrical advice. Confirm the exact regional model, care label, approved surface, solution, dilution, tank, tool, rinse and drying procedure before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Household upright liquid-dispensing and dirty-liquid-recovery appliance
keyFacts.evidence: Official pages describe solution delivery, agitation and suction recovery in household formats.
keyFacts.scope: Named upright models; spot-only and commercial machines excluded.

keyFacts.label: Chemical boundary
keyFacts.value: Use only exact-model approved solution and dilution
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer manuals and product pages specify proprietary or approved formulations and procedures.

systemFlow.name: Solution delivery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Clean tank, formula dosing, pump, tubing and spray jets
systemFlow.role: Delivers the documented liquid mixture to the target textile.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document model-specific tanks, formula and spray systems.

systemFlow.name: Agitation and recovery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Brush, nozzle, suction motor, dirty tank and separator
systemFlow.role: Loosens soil where designed and recovers liquid and debris.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers describe distinct brush and recovery architectures.

variants.name: Full-size upright washer
variants.operatorRelationship: User performs controlled wet and dry passes with the complete machine
variants.spaceConstraints: Tank filling, cord routing, furniture clearance and drying area
variants.limitations: Tank or motor size does not establish soil removal or drying time.
variants.evidence: BISSELL and Hoover publish full-size upright formats.

variants.name: Upright with integrated hose tools
variants.taskScale: Carpet plus stairs, upholstery and local stains
variants.operatorRelationship: User connects the exact hose and tool while the base supplies solution and recovery
variants.spaceConstraints: Hose reach, tool clearance and base stability
variants.limitations: Tool inclusion does not establish every fabric is wet-cleanable.
variants.evidence: Shark and Hoover publish integrated hose-tool configurations.

performanceMetrics.name: Soil-removal result
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Cleaning under a defined carpet, soil, solution and procedure
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Pretreatment, formula, passes, brush, recovery and test method must match
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not generalize a qualified ASTM comparison beyond its stated setup.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Shark declares ASTM F2828-based comparisons; ASTM publishes the method scope.

performanceMetrics.name: Residual moisture and drying
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Time and ventilation needed before returning the area to use
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Fiber, pile, passes, extraction, humidity and airflow differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Heat or fast-dry labels do not guarantee a universal drying time.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish qualified drying systems and instructions.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Trial the exact solution, pass sequence and recovery on a representative concealed area.
applicationFit.basis: Fiber, backing, soil, chemistry, agitation and extraction interact.
applicationFit.limitations: No universal stain, odor, colorfastness or drying result is provided.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Check care instructions and record solution, passes, recovered liquid and drying time.
applicationFit.evidence: Official product pages and manuals define exact procedures and surface boundaries.

applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Perform a concealed colorfastness and moisture trial with the exact tool.
applicationFit.basis: Tool spray, suction, fabric construction and base stability affect fit.
applicationFit.limitations: A hose tool does not make every textile wet-cleanable.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Confirm care code, solution, tool, extraction passes and ventilation.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers specify model-specific hose tools and approved areas.
applicationFit.scope: Exact delivered tool and approved textile.

componentStack.name: Solution and delivery system
componentStack.role: Stores, doses and sprays the approved liquid mixture.
componentStack.evidence: Official sources document materially different solution systems.

componentStack.name: Brush and recovery system
componentStack.role: Agitates where designed and recovers dirty liquid into a separate tank.
componentStack.evidence: Manufacturers publish distinct architectures and service procedures.

representativeModels.evidence: BISSELL publishes model 4117 data and qualified modes.
Hoover publishes the named product configuration.
Shark publishes model EX201 specifications and claim qualifications.

representativeModels.subtype: Upright carpet cleaner with hose tool

representativeModels.evidence: Kärcher publishes the exact product architecture and applications.
representativeModels.scope: Regional SE 6 Signature Line; not an upright body.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Textile approval, soil removal, residual moisture and drying
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Ranking by motor watts, brush count or fast-dry wording
procurementDecisions.assessment: Run a concealed representative-area trial with documented passes.
procurementDecisions.basis: Textile, chemistry, agitation, recovery and environment interact.
procurementDecisions.limitations: No catalogue feature guarantees a task result.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Record chemistry, passes, recovered liquid, texture and dry time.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources define model-specific systems and methods.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Solution, brush, belt, seals, tanks and hose availability
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming cleaning formulas or visual-fit parts are interchangeable
procurementDecisions.assessment: Attach approved chemistry and exact service codes to the quote.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain part and formula codes, prices, lead times and warranty terms.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official solution and product pages name exact compatibility.

engineeringChecks.reason: Wrong chemistry, moisture or agitation can affect fibers, backing, color and indoor exposure.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Check care label, manufacturer instructions, SDS where applicable and concealed-area test.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer sources restrict solution and surface use.

engineeringChecks.reason: Leaks, foam, blocked jets or weak recovery change results and drying.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Inspect seals and jets; verify rinsing, defoaming and storage procedures.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals document tank and cleaning procedures.

standards.name: ASTM F2828
standards.applicability: Laboratory method referenced by manufacturers for assessing cleaning effectiveness of household carpet-cleaning products.
standards.evidence: ASTM and Shark identify the method and qualified comparison use.
standards.scope: Use only with the exact edition, carpet, soil, solution and procedure.

developments.title: Shark dated its CarpetXpert comparative test baseline
developments.summary: Shark states its consumer-carpet-cleaner comparison used ASTM F2828 and included solution as of the stated date.
developments.evidence: Shark publishes the qualification on its official category page.
developments.scope: Shark comparison only; not a universal ranking.
